pr_title: sql: timestamp should accept DB2 formatted timestamps
pr_body:
fixes : #49768

This PR adds additional extracting field logics that
allow db2 formatted timesstamps to be parsed.

Release note (sql change): The pgdate util can now parse
db2 formatted timestamps. This can be used to import db2 dumps.

issue_context.title: sql: timestamp should accept DB2 formatted timestamps
issue_context.body:
DB2 timestamps use the following format:
2014-03-15-04.38.53.399853

Which differs from ours:
2014-03-15 04:38:53.399853

When trying to import data directly from a db2 dump file requires some pre-processing.  The DB2 format seems fairly straightforward and I can see no reason why we can't make this a valid insert format as well.

https://www.db2tutorial.com/db2-basics/db2-timestamp/
comments:

Oh, and we should also accept their default with TZ.

If we do not want to accept this timestamp type, then an alternative is to specify the format directly here or in the import statement.  Being able to specify the format directly is arguably better, but a lot more work.
I would love to take a look at this if no one else is working on it!

review_comments:
i'm reading https://www.db2tutorial.com/db2-basics/db2-timestamp/ and https://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSEPEK_10.0.0/sqlref/src/tpc/db2z_bif_timestamp.html
can you double check this works 
a) without timezones
b) seconds component of timezone working
c) no dashes between D and H
d) fractional digits, e.g. 	TIMESTAMP('2007-09-24-15.53.37.2162474',9);
a few error conditions, e.g. `2007-09-24-15.0` may also be nice to test.

this feels like it can conflict with the `case !fe.Wants(fieldSecond) && fe.Wants(fieldNanos):` below, where we want ms.
does it? should this be `fe.Wants(field.Minute) && !fe.Wants(fieldNanos)`, or that case moved up above this one? or even better, when we find a `-` separator between Day and Hour, we mark `isDB2` on an only trigger this on `isDB2 == true`? i can dig a bit more, but curious if you have a summary of why this is exhaustively ok ;)
You are right, using `isDB2` as a trigger prevents unnecessary field extraction.
should `fe.isDB2` already be set by the `-` separator below, or is the `-` between the YYYY-MM-DD and HH.MM.SS optional?

You could have something like `yyyy-mm-dd hh.mm.ss` which is a DB2 type, we need to set DB2 on `mm` so if we get something like `yyyy-mm-dd hh.mm:ss` we could throw an error. 

In this cause it won't have`-` but still should be treated as db2 timestamp.
